jobs.title: Youth Development Specialist, Alpha (Remote) - $120,000/year USD
jobs.description:
"All of my students came back in the top 1% for growth and achievement on their MAP scores."

— Sam DePalo, Lead Guide, Alpha Fort Worth Texas

Alpha is hiring.

Most youth development careers reward you for staying put. This one rewards you for arriving. You will land at a different Alpha campus every one to three months, walk in as a stranger to every student, parent and colleague, and have them working at full standard inside a week.

Alpha sends you where the network needs you, on site at campuses across the United States: one launching from nothing, or one running short-staffed. You do not choose the city. Accommodation is booked and paid for at every stop, and you earn a flat $120,000 wherever you live. You will be away from home every week outside of PTO.

Alpha is a private school where students finish core academics in two hours a day using adaptive software. The rest of the day goes to life skills: public speaking, focus, collaboration, and giving and taking feedback. You will not teach math or reading. You will run one-hour workshops where students build, debate and present, then coach them one to one against their own progress data until they hit their weekly targets.

Most people doing this work see one cohort in one city. You will see the whole network: which motivation strategies travel and which are local, and what separates a campus that is thriving from one that is struggling, because you will have worked in both inside the same year. You will also watch quiet students stand up and present to a room, in more than one state. Nothing prepares you faster to lead a campus of your own.

If the road is the point rather than the price, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Run one-hour life skill workshops for K-8 students, adapting the provided curriculum to the cohort in front of you
Coach students one to one and in small groups using Coachbot analytics, weekly goals and incentives, until 90% or more hit their targets
Administer and score Test2Pass assessments so students prove the skill rather than just attend the session
Reach full standard inside your first week at each new campus, with names learned and rapport built
Hand over cleanly at the end of every posting, documenting per-student progress and every open intervention

What You Won’t Be Doing

Teaching core academic subjects, lecturing from the front of the room, or grading
Writing curriculum from scratch: workshop plans, analytics and playbooks are provided
Running campus operations, facilities or admissions
Filling in as a substitute with no authority and no accountability for student results
Funding your own travel: accommodation is booked and paid for at every posting

Youth Development Specialist Key Responsibilities

Hold student outcomes at full standard at whichever campus is launching or running short-staffed.

Basic Requirements

Based anywhere in the US, within reasonable reach of a major airport
Willing to be posted away from home one to three months at a time, with time at home only during PTO
Comfortable with Alpha assigning every posting, including the city and the campus
Bachelor's degree in any subject
At least 3 years working with K-8 students. Classroom experience is not required: camp counseling, coaching and youth program leadership all count
Able to describe one specific time you coached a K-8 student toward a goal, including the goal, what you did, and the result
Legal right to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

A track record of sustained mobility: travel-heavy field roles, touring programs, seasonal camp circuits, or service-year placements across multiple cities
Experience running youth workshops in camps, athletics, enrichment programs or youth leadership settings
Comfort reading student progress dashboards or learning analytics to decide where to intervene
Experience coaching a disengaged student to a measurable improvement you can point to

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

Company Description
NAMI Santa Clara County is a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting individuals and families affected by mental illness in Santa Clara County. The organization provides practical experience, peer support, education, and understanding to those concerned about mental health conditions and their treatment. NAMI Santa Clara County collaborates with public agencies, private businesses, and media partners to increase awareness of effective treatment approaches. The organization actively advocates for expanded research and improved services for people living with mental illness, aiming to reduce stigma and promote recovery-focused care.

The Peer Support Specialist is a part-time, on-site role based in San Jose, CA. Personal lived experience with mental health conditions and recovery, with readiness to share that experience appropriately in a peer support context.
Knowledge of local mental health services, community resources, and recovery principles; prior experience in peer support, social services, or community outreach is beneficial.

Position Summary

The Community Wellness Department’s program goals include maximizing the quality of the member experience and clinical outcomes. This is achieved through an integrated, team-oriented, strengths-based holistic healthcare approach. CWD incorporates prevention, community-engagement and cultural-competence, and integration of behavioral health treatment with a particular focus on the local urban Native American community. This approach allows staff and trainees to develop their skills and creates an environment conducive to professional growth and intercultural proficiency.

The Program Manager I (PM I) provides management, support, and implementation of grants within the Community Wellness Department, across multiple sites, and may include supervision of staff members to execute a scope of work. The incumbent plays the primary role in the development and implementation of site programming to ensure attainment of successful internal and grant outcomes including improved community access, system navigation, program sustainability and integration of services. The PM I is responsible for facilitating implementation and delivery of culturally-based prevention activities and afterschool learning curriculum, including groups, cultural activities, and linkages to traditional knowledge and resources across both NAHC sites and with

collaborating partners. Additionally, the PM I will be responsible for supervision, leadership, and guidance to the CWD team and oversight of youth engagement and program development. This might also include supervision of volunteers and interns, financial management, event planning, and strategy development.

The Native American Health Center is an accredited institution and adheres to the standards of excellence set forth by the Accreditation Association of Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC) and the Commission of Dental Accreditation (CODA).

Duties And Responsibilities

PROGRAM MANAGEMENT: Responsible for envisioning and facilitating development of a program team, articulating its goals and strategy, and reporting

on its outputs.

Work with community and staff to determine unmet community services and program needs. Develop new funding, processes, curriculum, projects and

approaches in response. Facilitate community advisory councils and use information to inform work.

Communicate and collaborate with senior stakeholders to integrate and align CWD services across other NAHC departments and ensure compliance with

department, agency and funding agency regulations.

Analyze and improve workflow processes for the program.
Develop annual program work plans in achievement of the program goals and grant deliverables

actions to improve performance and build staff capacity.

Ensure meaningful participation by family, youth, and community members in prevention and evaluation processes via design, interpretation, and

dissemination of findings.

Represent the program in meetings, task forces, and partner collaborations.
Work in concert with Research and Evaluation team to ensure that all required data strategies, collection, and documentation of program objectives and

outcomes occur.

Assist in creation and implementation of methodologies, process improvements, and evaluation action plans to improve program operations, outcomes, and quality.
Work in concert with the Communications Team to ensure the social media and outreach strategy objectives are met. Develop compelling campaigns to further expand and promote services and visibility.
Responsible for promoting community events, groups, and other activities across multiple sites, across NAHC, and at outreach events.
Responsible for timely and accurate reporting and documentation of community events, groups, and program activities for regular reports to leadership and funders.

Serve as a representative of NAHC to grant funders and community stakeholders

operate in a timely and effective manner.

Provide leadership on program development and expansion of program activities
Refer participants and their families to appropriate community agencies or facilities; acts as liaison with such organizations and advocates for patients

and/or their families.

Setup trainings and classes for staff and community members on program specific knowledge to build skills and familiarity in specific program.

Become familiar with grant management and processes and procedures set forth by NAHC

Administer and score Test2Pass assessments so students prove the skill rather than just attend the session
Reach full standard inside your first week at each new campus, with names learned and rapport built
Hand over cleanly at the end of every posting, documenting per-student progress and every open intervention

Funding your own travel: accommodation is booked and paid for at every posting

Hold student outcomes at full standard at whichever campus is launching or running short-staffed.

Experience coaching a disengaged student to a measurable improvement you can point to
